title: Mango Chutney
subtitle: Sweet and tangy mango chutney with warm spices
excerpt: Ripe mangoes cooked down with vinegar, sugar, ginger, and spices into a thick, glossy, golden chutney. The essential accompaniment to a curry, a Scotch egg, or a mature Cheddar sandwich.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mango chutney was adopted into British cooking through the East India Company's trade with India in the 17th and 18th centuries. The Indian original is sharper and spicier; the British-style version is sweeter, cooked to a thick preserve. It became a standard British condiment, particularly associated with Coronation Chicken and as a curry accompaniment. Making it at home takes about an hour and produces a chutney far better than the commercial versions.

content.text: The chutney is ready when a wooden spoon drawn through the middle leaves a clear line that fills in slowly. It will thicken further as it cools. Sterilise jars by washing in hot soapy water, then placing in a 150 C oven for 15 minutes. Fill while the chutney and jars are both hot. Store sealed jars in a cool, dark place for up to a year; refrigerate once opened.

items.preparation: ripe, peeled and diced (about 800 g flesh)

content.text: Combine all the ingredients in a heavy-based saucepan. Stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.

Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook uncovered for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring regularly, until the mango is very soft and the mixture has thickened to a jam-like consistency. A spoon drawn across the base of the pan should leave a clear line.
Pour into sterilised jars while hot. Seal immediately. Leave to cool completely before storing. Refrigerate once opened.
